attempts.summary: Created the opsbot account on node1 and node2 (RHEL 7), generated an ed25519 keypair for opsbot on node1, installed the public key into opsbot's authorized_keys on node2, and locked the opsbot password on both nodes. Added a `Match User opsbot { PasswordAuthentication no; PubkeyAuthentication yes }` block to /etc/ssh/sshd_config on both nodes (the pre-existing global `PasswordAuthentication no` at the bottom of the file was actually a no-op since OpenSSH honors only the first occurrence of a keyword in the global context, which was `yes`). Verified opsbot@node1 can SSH to opsbot@node2 using the key with no password prompt, and that password-only auth attempts for opsbot are rejected on both nodes (server offers only publickey/gssapi). Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on both nodes: captured boot_id baselines, rebooted node1 then polled until reachable with a new boot_id, verified sshd/opsbot/keys/cross-node SSH recovered, then repeated for node2, and re-verified password auth is still rejected post-reboot on both nodes.
